registered_before: any timed measurement of the raw_tp/sys_exit token mode
what_happened: The first measurement (07/11 09:46-10:23, fexit mode, validation-evidence/results-20261107/token-probe-overhead/overhead.json) found open + close about 2.1-3.4 us slower than condition A when monitored and 1.8-2.1 us slower than off when NOT monitored, far above the BPF programs' own time (bpf_stats: 82-93 ns for the openat, close and security_file_open programs). A diagnostic (hookcost*.jsonl, PULSE_TOK_SKIP) showed the cost grows with the number of attached trampolines, even trampolines on syscalls the benchmark never calls, and /sys/kernel/tracing/enabled_functions showed __x64_sys_openat already hooked twice by Tetragon's kprobes, hence routed through arch_ftrace_ops_list_func, which walks every ftrace_ops (one per BPF trampoline).
change: loader --token-exit sys_exit (now the default): one raw_tp/sys_exit program gives the hooked calls' tokens at return, using the syscall number sys_enter stored in pulse_task_state and a tok_pending flag set at entry (seccomp-skipped calls reach sys_exit without running and give no second token). fentry/security_file_open stays (one ftrace_ops). Both modes pass scripts/token_probe_proof.py on k8s-worker1 with exactly one token per syscall (403,884 and 399,788 calls).

conditions_added.tokB, tokC, tokD, tokD_filtered: as registered, now in sys_exit mode
conditions_added.tokDfx: --tokens grams --token-exit fexit, benchmark monitored (the first measurement's tokD)

design: unchanged: 5 rounds on the three workers at the same time, conditions rotated each round, ready on 'attached' plus 1 s
decision: none (owner 06/11: measure and report). Both measurements are reported; the first one is not discarded.
